Kitap dünyasına açılan kapınızı aralayın! En sevdiğiniz kitapları indirimli fiyatlarla keşfedin ve hayal gücünüzü genişletin.
Bugün öğlen saatlerinde Muratpaşa ilçesi Yüksekalan Mahallesi 546. Sokak'ta bulunan 75. Yıl Cumhuriyet Anadolu Lisesi'nde meydana gelen olayda 10. sınıf öğrencisi E.V.K. (17), aynı sınıfta okuyan N.D.'yi (16) maket bıçağıyla boynundan, yüzünden ve vücudunun çeşitli yerlerinden yaraladı.
Olayın adından sınıfın penceresine çıkan E.V.K., 3. kattaki pencereden atladı. Durumun 112 Acil Çağrı Merkezi'ne bildirilmesi üzerine olay yerine çok sayıda polis ve sağlık ekibi sevk edildi. Maket bıçağı ile yaralanan N.D. ve 3. kattan atlayarak yaralanan E.V.K., sağlık ekiplerinin olay yerindeki ilk müdahalesinin ardından hastaneye kaldırıldı.
Olayı haber alan veliler okula koşarken, okul yönetimi ailesi gelen öğrencilerin okuldan çıkmasına izin verdi. Polis ekipleri olayla ilgili inceleme başlatırken, maket bıçaklı saldırı sonucu yaralanan N.D.'nin annesi konuştu.
Olayı haber alarak Antalya Eğitim Araştırma Hastanesi'ne kaldırılan kızının yanına gelen anne Gamze D., saldırıyı yapan E.V.K.'nın kızının sınıf arkadaşı olduğunu belirterek, "Aralarında hiçbir sorun yok. Kızımı tuvalete çekiyor. Önce bahçede bir tur atıyorlar. ‘Gel birlikte tuvalete gidelim' diyor. Bakıyorlar tuvaletin kapısı kilitli, kızım arkasını döndüğü an cebindeki maket bıçağını çıkarıp kızımı boynundan, yüzünden, sırtından yaralıyor. Kızım o anda zaten bayılmış. Şu anda kızım acil serviste yatıyor" dedi.
Maket bıçağının şah damarına yakın bir noktaya isabet ettiğini ve kızının tedavisinin sürdüğünü belirten Gamze D., "Doktorlar şah damarına gelmeye 1 santimetre kalmış diyor. Herhangi bir sorunu yoktu kızımın, büyük ihtimalle gözüne kestirdi. Kızım olmasa başkası da olabilirdi. Aralarında hiçbir sorun yok, kızımın sırf iyi niyetinden faydalanmış. Benim kızım sessiz sakin bir kızdı. Tuvalete çekiyor, arkasını dönünce saldırıyor. Biz okuldan çok memnunduk. Okulda disiplin iyi, müdürler ve öğretmenler iyi, okulda bir sorun yoktu" ifadelerini kullandı.
texts.https://www.bloomberght.com/crowdstrike-:
ABD merkezli siber güvenlik şirketi CrowdStrike , bulut tabanlı güvenlik şirketi Zscaler 'ı 43,9 milyar dolarlık tamamen hisse takasına dayalı bir anlaşmayla satın alacak. Siber güvenlik alanında kayıtlara geçen en büyük satın alma, yapay zekadaki ilerlemelerin siber tehditleri giderek karmaşıklaştırdığı bir dönemde sektörün iki büyük şirketini bir araya getiriyor.
Anlaşma, CrowdStrike'ın bilgisayar, sunucu ve diğer cihazlara yönelik koruma hizmetleriyle Zscaler'ın çalışanların uygulamalara ve verilere güvenli erişimini sağlayan teknolojisini birleştirecek. Böylece şirketler ve kamu kurumları için daha kapsamlı bir siber güvenlik platformu oluşturulacak.
Zscaler hisseleri yüzde 13'ün üzerinde yükselerek 220,52 dolara ulaştı. Buna rağmen hisselerin fiyatı, anlaşmada öngörülen hisse başına 260,41 dolarlık değerin belirgin biçimde altında kaldı. CrowdStrike hisseleri ise yaklaşık yüzde 12 geriledi.
IG Group Baş Teknik Analisti Axel Rodoplu, "İşlem büyüklüğü ve her iki şirketin önemi göz önüne alındığında, rekabet incelemesi kesinlikle mümkün. Ancak düzenleyicilerin işlemi mutlaka engellemeye çalışacağını varsaymak için henüz erken" dedi.
Rodoplu, "Asıl mesele muhtemelen düzenleyicilerin iki şirketin faaliyetleri arasında ne kadar örtüşme gördüğü ve bunun sonucunda müşterilerin gerçekten daha az rekabetçi alternatife sahip olup olmayacağı olacak" ifadelerini kullandı.
Satın alma, siber güvenlik sektöründeki konsolidasyon sürecinde gerçekleşiyor. Müşteriler hizmet aldıkları güvenlik sağlayıcılarının sayısını azaltmayı tercih ederken, şirketler de birden fazla hizmeti bir araya getiren kapsamlı platformlar geliştirmeye yöneliyor.
Anlaşma, CrowdStrike'a mevcut ürünlerini kullanmayan yaklaşık 8 bin Zscaler müşterisine ulaşma ve bu müşterilere kendi ürünlerini satma fırsatı sağlayacak. Zscaler'ın müşterileri arasında Unilever ve United Airlines gibi büyük şirketler de yer alıyor.
Dünya genelinde şirketlerin daha karmaşık saldırılarla karşılaşması, siber güvenlik araçlarına yönelik talebi artırdı. Yapay zekadaki ilerlemeler, yazılım açıklarının tespit edilmesini ve istismar edilmesini kolaylaştırırken tehditleri belirleyip engelleyen araçların gelişmesine de katkı sağlıyor.
texts.https://tr.euronews.com/2026/11/23/crowd:
ABD merkezli siber güvenlik şirketi CrowdStrike, rakibi Zscaler'i pazartesi günü 43,9 milyar dolar (40,4 milyar euro) karşılığında satın aldı. Böylece bugüne kadarki en büyük siber güvenlik anlaşmasıyla bulut tabanlı siber güvenlik hizmetlerini tek bir hizmet sağlayıcı altında toplayarak müşterilere ortak bir adres sunmayı hedefliyor.
Şirketlerin bulut siber güvenlik sektöründe birlikte çalışma geçmişi uzun. CrowdStrike cihaz koruması sunarken Zscaler, ağ trafiğini ve uygulama erişimini siber tehdit ve saldırılara karşı güvence altına alıyor.
Birleşme, son aylarda siber olayların ve altyapıya yönelik tehditlerin sıradan hale geldiği bir dönemde gerçekleşiyor.
Eylülden bu yana Avrupa, market buzdolaplarını hedef alan siber saldırılarla karşı karşıya kaldı. Kripto cüzdan şirketi Binance, Kuzey Koreli hackerların hedefi oldu. Bir Google Cloud kesintisi Revolut dahil finansal hizmetler şirketlerini devre dışı bıraktı. Microsoft'un sunucuları çöktü ve Outlook, Teams ile diğer platformlar kullanılamaz hale geldi. Bunlar yalnızca birkaç örnek.
CrowdStrike'ın kendisi de 2024'te, bir yazılım hatasının dünya genelinde yaklaşık 8,5 milyon Microsoft Windows cihazının çökmesine yol açmasıyla bir siber güvenlik sorununun merkezinde yer almıştı. Bunun sonucunda uçuşlar iptal edilmiş, hastaneler kapatılmış, bankalar ve diğer hizmetler dünya çapında aksamıştı.
Bu tabloya ek olarak, yapay zeka, internetin temelini oluşturan yazılımlarda ve PHP ile Java dahil programlama dillerinde yeni siber güvenlik açıkları ortaya çıkardı.
CrowdStrike'ın şirketi satın alma kararında, aralarında Zero Trust Exchange sisteminin de bulunduğu yapay zeka sistemlerindeki uzmanlığı belirleyici oldu. Bu sistem kurumsal yapay zeka kullanımını güvence altına alıyor, yapay zeka iş akışlarındaki hassas verileri koruyor ve yapay zeka uygulamalarını ile ajanlarını gerçek zamanlı olarak yönetiyor.
CrowdStrike CEO'su ve kurucusu George Kurtz, "Ağ eskiden insanları mekanlara bağlardı. Artık ajanları veriye bağlıyor. Zscaler ile siber güvenliğin işletim sistemini inşa ediyoruz: yapay zekayı devreye almak, yapay zekayı kontrol etmek ve herhangi bir ajan temelli uygulamanın güvenli şekilde çalışmasını sağlamak için tek bir kontrol düzlemi oluşturuyoruz," dedi.
Pazartesi günü yayımlanan basın bülteninde şirketler, anlaşma için bir dizi gerekçe sıraladı. Bunlar arasında cihaz ve ağ veri güvenliğini birleştirme potansiyeli, müşteri tabanları arasında çapraz satış imkanları yaratmak, pazarları ve ekosistemleri genişletmek ve en önemlisi müşterilere ortak, tek bir çözüm sunmak yer aldı.
Kurtz, "Dünyanın bugüne kadar gördüğü en büyük yapay zeka güvenliği ve siber güvenlik şirketi haline gelebileceğimiz bir yol görüyoruz," diye ekledi.
Şirketler, anlaşmanın toplam hedeflenebilir pazarlarını 185 milyar dolardan (168,7 milyar euro) fazla artırmasını bekliyor. Bu sayede CrowdStrike'ın platformu yaklaşık 8 bin Zscaler müşterisine ulaşacak ve birleşik yıllık yinelenen gelirlerine tahminen 10 milyar dolar (9,1 milyar euro) daha eklenecek.
Anlaşma uyarınca CrowdStrike, Zscaler'i tamamen hisse karşılığı bir işlemle, şirketin 20 Kasım 2026 Cuma günü oluşan hisse fiyatı üzerinden satın alacak.
CrowdStrike, işlemi Zscaler hissedarlarının onayına bağlı olarak 2028'de tamamlamayı bekliyor. Anlaşmaya göre Zscaler CEO'su Jay Chaudhry şirketin başında kalacak ve CrowdStrike'ın yönetim kuruluna katılacak.

A Milli Erkek Basketbol Takımı Kaptanı Kenan Sipahi , FIBA 2027 Basketbol Dünya Kupası Elemeleri'nde oynayacakları İtalya ve İzlanda maçlarından galibiyetle ayrılmak istediklerini söyledi.
A Erkek Milli Basketbol Takımı, FIBA 2027 Basketbol Dünya Kupası Elemeleri İkinci Tur J Grubu üçüncü maçında 26 Kasım Perşembe günü TSİ 22.00'de Roma'da İtalya ile, pencerenin diğer maçında ise 29 Kasım Pazar günü saat 19.00'da Turkcell Basketbol Gelişim Merkezi'nde İzlanda ile karşı karşıya gelecek.
Milliler, karşılaşmalar öncesinde Turkcell Basketbol Gelişim Merkezi'nde düzenlenen basın toplantısında medya mensuplarıyla bir araya geldi.
Toplantıda açıklamalarda bulunan A Milli Erkek Basketbol Takımı Kaptanı Kenan Sipahi, yaz döneminde Dünya Kupası elemelerinde önemli galibiyetler aldıklarını belirterek, "İtalya'ya karşı ve İzlanda'ya karşı oynayacağız. Aslında yazın garantilemiş olmamız bu açıdan çok önemliydi. Eksik olacağımızı biliyorduk, NBA oyuncularımızın olmayacağını biliyorduk. O yüzden yazın olan maçlara çok önem vermiştik. Tabii beklemediğimiz birkaç sakatlığımız da oldu. Kaptanımız Cedi Osman'ın da sakatlığıyla beraber bu kadro öncekilere göre daha eksik ama hedefimiz yine değişmeyecek. İlk önce İtalya'da, sonra da evimizde oynayacağımız İzlanda maçlarından galibiyetle ayrılmak istiyoruz. İnşallah başarırız" dedi.
Milli takım takviminin oyuncular açısından zorlayıcı olduğunu dile getiren Sipahi, "Bu program oyuncular için aslında çok zorlayıcı oluyor. Özellikle EuroLeague'de oynayan oyuncular için daha da zorlayıcı. Bazen bir akşam önce oynadıktan sonra milli maça gelmeleri gerekiyor. Mental olarak biraz zorlanıyoruz ama milli forma olduğu zaman yorgunluklar gidiyor. Çünkü biz birlikte vakit geçirmeyi çok seven bir kadroyuz. Birlikte oynamayı, sahada mücadele etmeyi birlikte başarmış bir kadroyuz. Bunu aynı şekilde bir iki maç için en iyi şekilde hazırlanmaya çalışacağız" ifadelerini kullandı.
Dünya sıralamasında daha üst basamaklara çıkmayı hedeflediklerini aktaran Kenan Sipahi, "Temel motivasyon olarak biz dünya sıralamasında da daha yükselmek istiyoruz. Bu açıdan bizi motive eden en büyük şeylerden biri o. Tabii o yüzden galibiyetlere devam etmek istiyoruz aynı şekilde. Ama bu sezonun bu bölümünde de aynı zamanda sağlıklı kalmamız gerekiyor. Dünya sıralamasındaki bu mücadeleyi vereceğimiz için motivasyonumuz çok da azalmıyor. Özellikle milli formayı giydiğinizde ne olursa olsun, hazırlık maçı dahi olsun, her zaman yüksek motivasyon ve duygusal olarak da yüksek maçlar oynuyorsunuz. Dediğim gibi bizim için bir şey fark etmeyecek" şeklinde konuştu.
Genç oyuncuların A Milli Takım'a uyum sağlaması için tecrübeli isimler olarak örnek olmaya çalıştıklarını söyleyen milli basketbolcu, "Biz nasıl daha önce aynı şekilde genç oyuncu olduysak büyüklerimiz bize iyi örnek olmaya çalıştı. Sahada, hem saha içi hem saha dışında, hem bireysel olarak hazırlanma açısından hem mücadele olarak nasıl örnek oldularsa biz de aynı şekilde onlara örnek olmaya çalışıyoruz. Zaten yazın Ömer Kutluay da olsun, bence bizim A Milli Takım'da yavaş yavaş oynamaya hazır olduğunu, olduklarını gösteriyorlar. Bu maçlarla beraber garantilemiş olmamızla beraber onların da yavaş yavaş adapte olmasını umuyoruz" diye konuştu.

Trendyol Süper Lig ’in 12’nci haftasında İstanbul Başakşehir FK, sahasında Çorum FK ile karşı karşıya geldi. Mücadeleyi hakem Direnç Tonusluoğlu yönetti. Tonusluoğlu’nun yardımcılıklarını Esat Sancaktar ve Hüseyin Aylak yaptı.
Teknik direktör Nuri Şahin yönetimindeki İstanbul Başakşehir FK , Çorum FK karşısında sahaya; Muhammed Şengezer, Saba Kharebashvili, Jerome Opoku, Emin Bayram, Michal Karbownik, Jakub Kaluzinski, Olivier Kemen, Ivan Brnic, Andreas Skov Olsen, Eldor Shomurodov ve Davie Selke ilk 11’iyle çıktı.
Teknik direktör Burak Yılmaz yönetimindeki Çorum FK ise mücadeleye; Erhan Erentürk, Alexandre Penetra, Çağlar Söyüncü, Hrvoje Smolcic, Andrei Borza, Ylber Ramadani, Mohamed Diomande, Göktan Gürpüz, Alexandros Kyziridis, Markus Karlsbakk ve Jesus Ramirez ilk 11’iyle başladı.
18’inci dakikada Başakşehir’de Emin Bayram, sakatlığı nedeniyle oyuna devam edemedi. Sedyeyle saha dışına alınan Bayram, karşılaşmadan çıkmak zorunda kaldı.
29’uncu dakikada Çorum FK’nın kontra atağında Smolcic’in orta sahadan savunmanın arkasına gönderdiği topla buluşan Ramirez, rakip yarı saha boyunca topu sürdü. Kaleciyle karşı karşıya kalan Ramirez, aşırtma vuruşla topu ağlara gönderdi: 0-1.
31’inci dakikada sağ kanattan yapılan ortada arka direkte topla buluşan Selke’nin kafa vuruşunda kaleci Erhan Erentürk gole izin vermedi.
52’nci dakikada sağ kanattan yapılan ortada iyi yükselen Selke’nin kafa vuruşunda top direğe çarparak dışarı çıktı.
55’inci dakikada Kharebashvili’nin ceza sahası dışından çektiği sert şutta top az farkla dışarı çıktı.
68’inci dakikada Borza’nın sol kanattan yaptığı ortada Mahmic, topu ağlara gönderdi: 0-2.
74’üncü dakikada Umut Bozok’un ceza sahası yayı gerisinden verdiği pasla çaprazdan ceza sahasına giren Brnic’in vuruşunda top direkten döndü.
77’nci dakikada sol kanatta topla buluşan Shomurodov’un ortasında top savunmadan döndü. Seken topu göğsüyle kontrol eden Shomurodov, çok uzak mesafeden yaptığı şık vuruşla topu ağlara gönderdi: 1-2.
82’nci dakikada Onur Bulut’un sağ kanattan yaptığı ortada arka direkte yükselen Bertuğ Yıldırım, kafa vuruşuyla topu kalenin sağından ağlara gönderdi: 2-2.
87’nci dakikada Brnic’in sol kanattan yaptığı ortada penaltı noktası üzerinde yükselen Bertuğ Yıldırım, kafa vuruşuyla topu filelerle buluşturarak takımını öne geçirdi: 3-2.
90+1’inci dakikada Karbownik’in sol kanattan verdiği pasla ceza sahası yayı üzerinde topla buluşan Bertuğ Yıldırım, yaptığı vuruşla topu ağlara gönderdi: 4-2.
Maç İstanbul Başakşehir FK'nın 4-2'lik üstünlüğüyle sona erdi.
Başakşehir’de 69’uncu dakikada oyuna dahil olan Bertuğ Yıldırım, karşılaşmanın 90+1’inci dakikasında hat-trick yaparak takımının geri dönüşünde önemli rol oynadı. Süper Lig’in 12’nci haftası öncesinde bu sezon golü bulunmayan 24 yaşındaki futbolcu, Çorum FK karşısında attığı 3 golle takımına galibiyeti getiren isim oldu.

Gündemi BBC Türkçe'den takip etmek artık WhatsApp'ta da mümkün. Haberlerimizin doğrudan telefonunuza gelmesi için tıklayın.
Oxfam yardım kuruluşunun yeni bir raporuna göre, İsrail saldırıları nedeniyle Gazze, yüzde 99'undan fazlasında çevre kirliliği görülen bir "zehirli çorak araziye" dönüştü.
Raporda, ağır metallerin, patlayıcı kalıntılarının, yıkılan binalardan kaynaklanan asbestin, dioksinlerin ve biyolojik atıkların Filistinliler için tehdit oluşturduğu belirtiliyor.
Bu tehdidin hem şu an geçerli olduğu hem de gelecek onlarca yılda devam etmesinin beklendiği ifade ediliyor.
Oxfam International'ın genel müdürü Amitabh Behar, bu etkinin Gazze'deki "insan güvenliği ve hayatta kalması için gerekli çevresel koşulları temelden bozacağını" söyledi.
İsrail'in İngiltere Büyükelçiliği ise bu raporun "profesyonel standartların altında kaldığını" söyledi.
Behar İsrail'i "Gazze'de devam eden soykırımın bir parçası olarak çevresel savaş suçları" işlemekle de suçladı.
İsrail, Uluslararası Adalet Divanı'nda devam eden davada kendisine yöneltilen soykırım suçlamalarını asılsız ve çarpıtılmış olarak reddediyor.
İsrail, Gazze'deki askeri harekatının, Hamas'ın 7 Ekim 2023'te İsrail'e düzenlediği ölümcül saldırıya karşılık bir öz savunma eylemi olduğunu ve sivillerin zarar görmesini azaltmak için adımlar attığını savunuyor.
Oxfam ve İngiltere merkezli Çatışma ve Çevre Gözlemevi (CEOBS), Gazze'deki üç yıllık yoğun savaşın yol açtığı ciddi çevresel etkiler konusunda bugüne kadarki en kapsamlı raporu hazırladı.
Bunun için uydu görüntüleri, uzaktan algılama, mekansal analiz ve diğer açık kaynak verilerini kullandı.
Raporda, İsrail'in yoğun bombardımanında kullanılan mühimmatın yanı sıra yıkılan binalardan ve altyapıdan kalan enkazın da çevre üzerindeki etkileri ayrıntılı olarak ele alınıyor.
Şubat 2026'da, bir Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) özel raportörü, Gazze'ye yaklaşık iki yılda 200.000 tondan fazla patlayıcı atıldığını ve bunun "yaklaşık 13 Hiroşima tipi nükleer bombanın toplam enerjisine eşdeğer" olduğunu belirtti.
Geçtiğimiz yıl, BM Çevre Programı (UNEP) tahminleri, İsrail'in evleri ve altyapıyı yok eden askeri operasyonlarının ülke genelinde 61 milyon tondan fazla enkaz oluşturduğunu ve bunun yaklaşık %15'inin tehlikeli maddelerden kaynaklanan yüksek kirlenme riski taşıdığını gösteriyordu.
Oxfam raporunun yazarı Lama Abdul Samad BBC'ye, "Bu kirleticilerin çoğu çevrede kalıcı olduğu için uzun vadeli kronik sağlık etkileri olacak" dedi.
Gazzelilerin şu anda ve gelecekte solunum yolu hastalıklarında, kanserlerde, organ hasarlarında ve doğum kusurları ile ölü doğumlarda artış yaşama olasılığının yüksek olduğunu söyledi.
Gazze'deki altı atıksu arıtma tesisinin tamamının devre dışı kalması nedeniyle, arıtılmamış kanalizasyon suları şu anda yeraltı sularına ve Akdeniz'e karışıyor.
Sağlık üzerindeki olumsuz etkiler, son zamanlarda şiddetli kış fırtınaları nedeniyle yağmur sularının atık sularla karışarak sokaklardan ve yerinden edilmiş insanların yaşadığı çadır alanlarından akmasıyla daha da kötüleşti.
Gazze'deki laboratuvarların yıkılması ve İsrail'in uzman test ekipmanlarının ve bilim insanlarının girişine getirdiği kısıtlamalar nedeniyle, kirlilik türleri ve seviyelerinin test edilmesi genellikle mümkün olmuyor.
BBC, konuyla ilgili yorum almak için İsrail ordusuyla iletişime geçti.
UNEP, güvenlik endişelerinin de personelinin daha önce Gazze'ye seyahat etmesini engellediğini belirtti.
Oxfam raporu, temizlik çalışmalarından önce kirlenme risklerini belirlemek için Gazze'de tam ve bağımsız bir çevre değerlendirmesi yapılmasını talep ediyor.
Raporda, çalışmalara katılan işçilerin korunmasına özel önem verilmesi gerektiği belirtiliyor.
Uydu görüntülerine ve doğrulanmamış varsayımlara dayandığını ve metodolojisinin ciddi bir incelemeye dayanmak için gereken akademik titizlikten yoksun olduğunu savundu.
Raporda, Hamas'ın kazdığı yüzlerce kilometrelik tünelleri dikkate almadan Gazze'nin toprak ve yer altı suları hakkında sonuçlar çıkardığı ve bu nedenle temelden kusurlu olduğu belirtildi.
Gazze'deki doktorlar, yıkılan binalardan ve yerinden edilmiş insanların ısınmak ve yemek pişirmek için plastik, bez ve karton yakmalarından kaynaklanan toz ve kirlilik nedeniyle akut solunum yolu enfeksiyonlarında artış olduğunu bildiriyor.
Sindirim sistemi hastalıkları ise güvenli olmayan su ve kötü hijyen koşullarıyla bağlantılı.
Filistinli dermatolog Dr. Alaa Abu Hajar, BBC'ye savaşın başlamasından bu yana kronik cilt hastalıklarında beş kat artış gördüğünü söyledi.
Bunu çevresel kirliliğe ve çadırlarda ve mülteci kamplarındaki aşırı kalabalık, hijyenik olmayan yaşam koşullarına bağladığını ekledi:
"Sokaklarda kemirgenler, çöpler ve kanalizasyon atıkları her yere yayılmış durumda. Ne yazık ki, en çok etkilenenler çocuklar."
Çiftçiler ve balıkçılıkla uğraşanlar, toprak ve deniz kirliliğinin güvenli gıda üretmelerini imkansız hale getirdiğini söylüyor.
Balıkçı Ebu el-Abed Sultan, "Kanalizasyon ve atık sular arıtılmadan denize boşaltılıyor ve bu büyük bir felaket" diyor ve ekliyor:
"Ayrıca yıkılan evlerden kalan molozlar da denize dökülüyor. Ağlarımızı indirdiğimizde moloz ve çöpleri yakalıyoruz. Bu deniz ortamına zarar veriyor; balıklar da etkileniyor, balıkçılar da."
Gazze sağlık bakanlığının verilerine göre, savaşın başlangıcından bu yana en az 74.746 Filistinli öldürüldü.
BM, insani koşulların vahim olmaya devam ettiğini belirtiyor.
İsrail, Gazze'nin geniş çaplı yeniden inşasını Hamas ve diğer Filistinli silahlı grupların tamamen silahsızlandırılması şartına bağladı.

Ermenistan, Azerbaycan ile barışın önünü açmayı hedefleyen yeni anayasa taslağını yayımladı. Taslakta Bakü'nün itiraz ettiği Karabağ maddesine ek olarak "soykırımın tanınması" çağrısı ve Ağrı Dağı da yer almadı.
Onlarca yıllık savaş sürecinin ardından Azerbaycan ile Ermenistan arasında barışa doğru önemli bir adım daha atıldı.
Erivan yönetimi, Azerbaycan ile kapsamlı bir barış anlaşmasının önünü açması beklenen yeni anayasa taslağını hazırladı. Taslakta, Dağlık Karabağ üzerinde hak iddiasına ilişkin ifadeler yer almadı.
Mevcut anayasada Ermenistan'ın sembolleri arasında sayılan ve bu nedenle Türkiye ile sorun yaşanmasına yol açan "Ararat" (Ağrı Dağı) da yeni metinden çıkarıldı. Anayasa taslağında ayrıca, "soykırımın uluslararası alanda tanınması" çağrısını içeren cümleye yer verilmedi.
Ülkede anayasa değişikliği için referandunma gidilmesi gerekiyor.
Ermenistan Başbakanı Nikol Paşinyan , taslağın yayınlanmasının ardından yaptığı ulusa sesleniş konuşmasında, yeni anayasanın kabul edilmesi hâlinde Azerbaycan ile barış anlaşmasının imzalanıp onaylanacağını, iki ülke arasında "kurumsal, kalıcı ve geri döndürülemez" barışın tesis edileceğini belirtti.
Yeni anayasa metninin " başka biri için veya dış baskıyla" hazırlanmadığını vurgulayan Paşinyan, "Halk anayasaya karşı oy kullanırsa istifa edeceğim" dedi ve erken seçime gidileceğini söyledi.
Başbakan, referandumda anayasanın kabul edilmesi hâlinde ise bir sonraki seçimlere aday olmayacağını açıkladı.
Referanduma gidilebilmesi için parlamentoda üçte iki çoğunluğun sağlanması gerekiyor. Bu kapsamda Paşinyan'ın liderliğindeki Sivil Sözleşme Partisi'nin en az altı muhalefet milletvekilinin desteğini alması gerekiyor. Taslağın ayrıca kamuoyunda kapsamlı bir tartışma sürecinden geçmesi öngörülüyor.
Ancak Ermenistan'daki başlıca muhalefet partileri anayasa taslağına şu ana kadar destek vermedi. Paşinyan, geçen Haziran'daki seçimler öncesinde de, özellikle Azerbaycan'ın 2023'te Karabağ'ı yeniden kontrol altına aldığı askeri operasyonun ardından yoğun eleştirilere maruz kalmıştı. Muhalefet ve toplumun bir kesimi, Paşinyan'ı Azerbaycan karşısında taviz vermekle suçluyor.
İki komşu ülke Ermenistan ile Azerbaycan arasında, büyük ölçüde Dağlık Karabağ anlaşmazlığı nedeniyle yakın dönemde şiddetli çatışmalar yaşanmıştı.
Dağlık Karabağ uzun yıllar Ermenilerin kontrolünde kalmış, Azerbaycan 2023 yılında düzenlediği askeri operasyonla bölgenin kontrolünü yeniden ele geçirmişti. Sonrasında bölgedeki Ermeni nüfusun tamamına yakını evlerini terk etmek ve Ermenistan'a göç etmek zorunda kaldı.
Taraflar, geçen yıl ABD'nin desteklediği ortak barış deklarasyonunu imzalarken, bu tarihten sonra ticari bağların yeniden kurulmasına yönelik adımlar atmış ve "gerçek barış" ortamında olduklarını açıklamıştı.

Oxfam’ın ve Çatışma ve Çevre Gözlemevi’nin (CEOBS) hazırladığı rapora göre İsrail’in saldırıları Gazze genelinde havayı, suyu ve toprağı kirleterek kuşaklar boyu toparlanamayacak bir yıkıma yol açtı.
The Guardian’ın aktardığı rapora göre İsrail’in Gazze’ye saldırıları çevre felaketine yol açtı, Filistinlilerin temel kaynaklarını mahvetti.
Uydu görüntüleri ve bilimsel analizlere dayanan rapora göre ağır metaller, patlayıcı kalıntıları, asbest ve kanalizasyon atıkları halk sağlığını on yıllarca olumsuz etkilemeyi sürdürebilir.
Oxfam International İcra Direktörü Amitabh Behar, ”İsrail’in Gazze’deki soykırımı, Gazze’nin çevresindeki saldırıları da kapsıyor. Bunlar, kuşaklar boyu yaşamı tehdit edecek çevresel savaş suçları” dedi.
Behar’a göre İsrail uluslararası insancıl hukuk ve insan hakları hukuku kapsamındaki yükümlülüklerini açıkça ihlal ediyor: ”Gazze’de yaşayan Filistinliler hava, gıda ve su yoluyla, ayrıca kirlenmiş toprak ve enkazla doğrudan temas ederek zehirli maddelere maruz kalıyor.”
Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) Uluslararası Soruşturma Komisyonu 2025’te ve 2026’nın başında İsrail’in Gazze’de soykırım suçu işlediğini, başbakan Binyamin Netanyahu dahil olmak üzere İsrailli yetkililerin soykırımı kışkırttığını tespit etti.
Netanyahu ayrıca savaş suçları nedeniyle Uluslararası Ceza Mahkemesi’nce (UCM) tutuklama kararıyla aranıyor.
İsrail’se komisyonun bulgularını ‘iftira niteliğinde düzmece’ diyerek reddediyor.
Oxfam’ın raporu 74 binden fazla Filistinliyi öldüren ve en az 175 bin kişiyi yaralayan İsrail’in geride bıraktığı ‘zehirli çorak arazi’ yi ayrıntılı ortaya koyuyor. Binlerce Filistinli hala kayıp.
Behar, ‘ ‘Arıtılmamış kanalizasyon suyu denize akıyor, toprağa sızıyor” dedi ve şöyle ekledi: ”Gazze’deki kanalizasyon ve arıtma sistemlerinin yıkılması, insanları kirliliğe karşı büyük ölçüde korumasız bırakıyor.”
BM Çevre Programı’na (UNEP) göre İsrail Gazze’de 61 milyon tonu aşkın enkaz oluşturdu. Yıkılan evler, mahalleler ve altyapı ciddi ölçüde tehlikeli maddelerin biriktiği alanlara dönüştü.
Raporun yazarı ve Oxfam’ın su ve sanitasyon uzmanı Lama Abdülsamed, kirliliğin kentlerdeki enkaza, tarım arazilerine, su sistemlerine ve toprağa yayılması nedeniyle Gazze’deki çevre hasarını gidermenin son derece güç olacağını söyledi.
Abdülsamed’e göre patlamamış mühimmat nedeniyle bölgelere erişmek zor.
Behar şöyle dedi: ”Çevre kirliliğinin ölçüsünü anlamadan ve bu sırada kirliliği gidermek için harekete geçmeden Gazze’yi yeniden inşa etmek, halk sağlığını kuşaklar boyu olumsuz etkileyecek sonuçlar doğurabilir.”

İstanbul'da otoparklarda "İlk 3 saat ücretsiz" kuralına uymayan 50 alışveriş, iş ve ticaret merkezine toplam 2 milyon 426 bin 775 lira ceza uygulandı.
İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesinden yapılan açıklamaya göre, İBB Zabıta Dairesi Başkanlığı, Ulaşım Koordinasyon Merkezinin (UKOME) yürürlükteki kararı doğrultusunda İstanbul genelindeki alışveriş, iş ve ticaret merkezi otoparklarındaki denetimlerini sürdürüyor.
İBB ekipleri yaptıkları denetimlerde, bu merkezlerin otoparklarında ilk üç saatlik (0-3 saat) kullanımın ücretsiz olması gerekirken 50 alışveriş, iş ve ticaret merkezinin bu kurala uymadığını tespit etti.
Denetimlerde son bir hafta içinde kurala uymayan ve İstanbulluları mağdur eden işletmelere yönelik 655 adet idari yaptırım tutanağı düzenlendi.
Bu kapsamda toplam 2 milyon 426 bin 775 lira tutarında cezai işlem uygulandı.
İBB, kurala aykırı uygulama yapan işletmecilere ve yönetimlere, UKOME kararına uygun davranmaları gerektiğini bildiren resmi yazılar gönderdi.
Yürütülen bilgilendirme ve denetim çalışmaları sonucunda 14 alışveriş ve ticaret merkezi, ilk üç saatlik otopark kullanımının ücretsiz olduğunu gösteren tarife listelerini otopark girişlerine ve ödeme noktalarına asarak uygulamalarını mevzuata uygun hale getirdi.
İstanbul'da alışveriş ve ticaret merkezi otoparklarında ilk üç saat ücretsiz uygulamasına aykırı bir durumla karşılaşan İstanbullular, İBB Çözüm Merkezine şikayette bulunabiliyor.
Bu kurala aykırı şekilde ücret talep eden işletmeler hakkında İBB Zabıta ekipleri tespit tutanağı düzenliyor.
Tutanaklar, idari para cezası kararı alınmak üzere İBB Encümen Müdürlüğüne bildiriliyor. 2026 yılı itibarıyla araç başına 3 bin 705 lira idari para cezası uygulanıyor.

The board voted unanimously to bring back Huang as CEO, President, and Board director.
Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO. The company announced on Monday morning that the board “voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA.”
In its statement, the board says that it received input “from senior levels of the United States government” and determined that “Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” Donald Trump responded to the board’s decision in a post on Truth Social , saying Nvidia “made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO… The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”
The board’s statement says that its investigation into reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot will continue, with Huang’s support and cooperation, while interim CEO Colette Kress will continue as CFO, and Harvey Jones will remain as the recently appointed board chair.
“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.” This move comes after Jones said during an earnings call last week that the Nvidia board “does not intend” to return Huang as CEO.
Huang resigned as CEO earlier this month following reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including an executive who reported to him. In the wake of his departure, more than 200,000 people, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, signed a letter to Nvidia’s board, calling for his reinstatement.
Nvidia shares tumbled in Huang’s absence , while industry analysts raised concerns about an outsider replacing him at a time when Nvidia is so critical to the AI boom . Nonetheless, the board maintained as recently as last Tuesday that Huang wasn’t coming back.
texts.https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/23/nvidia-j:
Nvidia on Monday announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO , effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries.
The board of directors said it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him. The board added that it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk."
President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump said he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard."
Huang resigned from his role as chief executive earlier this month after a series of shocking reports about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The New York Times reported on Sunday that the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security during at least part of the time that she was engaging in a relationship with Huang.
Shares of Nvidia surged 33% following Huang's reinstatement. The stock had shed nearly 33% from the time Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on Nov. 8. The stock closed at $186.64 on Nov.6.
"I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang said in a statement. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process."
Senior government officials briefed Nvidia's board late last week and communicated that no national security laws were violated, according to sources familiar with the discussion who asked to remain anonymous because they were not authorized to speak publicly. That update prompted the board to reach out to Huang, the people said.
Huang and the board held their first conversations since his ouster on Saturday, and the group determined he would return as CEO during a second meeting on Sunday, the people said. Nvidia's cratering stock price played a role in accelerating those conversations.
Trump celebrated Huang's return to Nvidia on Monday, writing in a post on his social media site that the board made "the correct and proper decision" to reinstate him. Trump said the U.S. needs Huang's leadership to "ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy."
He reiterated that the U.S. government has "no reason to believe" Huang's return poses a risk to national security, and that it "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct."
"On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," Trump wrote.
Several tech industry leaders, including Elon Musk , CEO of SpaceX , Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer at Atreides Management, and Brad Gerstner, Altimeter Capital CEO, had been actively lobbying for Huang's return. Musk wrote in a post on X on Monday that the board's "mistake has been corrected."
Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.
For weeks following Huang's ouster, the company's board maintained that it was not considering Huang's reinstatement. It appointed Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer, as the chipmaker's interim CEO, who reiterated that position in an interview with CNBC following Huang's exit. Kress will continue to serve as Nvidia's CFO, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Nvidia's board formed an independent committee and hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation into Huang and whether company secrets or national security were compromised. The board said Monday that "the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion" and that Huang is "committed to cooperating with it."
"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board chair, Harvey Jones, said in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company."
Even with Huang back at the helm, Nvidia is facing increased scrutiny over its chip sales in Southeast Asia and China.
Lawmakers have been preparing for investigations into how Huang's affair with the alleged spy may have damaged U.S. AI dominance, influenced his positions on export controls, and impacted his close relationships with Trump and his Cabinet. Huang has been one of the loudest voices opposing strict export controls on advanced chips.
"The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., said in a statement Monday.
Huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, is scheduled to appear before the panels on Dec. 2. Those dates were set before Huang's return, and John Fisher, who represents Huang, did not comment on whether there are any changes in his plans to testify.
Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott, R-S.C., said Monday that Huang will publicly testify on Dec. 3 as the sole witness during a hearing titled, "Protecting America's AI Advantage: Oversight of U.S. Export Controls."
"Americans deserve answers about what NVIDIA and the Trump administration knew, when they knew it, and whether sufficient steps were taken to prevent sensitive technology from falling into the wrong hands," Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., a member of the Banking Committee, wrote in a post on X on Monday.

In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy.
The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk.
Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET.
In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security.
Trump also said the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity.
A long list of high-profile tech executives were pushing the board — in social media posts and publicly aired interviews — to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Atoms founder Travis Kalanick, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whom signed a petition pushing for reinstatement.
The company said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.”
Just a few days ago, the board had seemed immovable in its choice to push Huang out. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey C. Jones said they didn’t intend to reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement.
Jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones said the board believes Huang is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of its stockholders, employees, partners, and customers.
“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company,” Jones said. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.”
In a statement, Huang said he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993.
“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”

Jensen Huang is returning to Nvidia as chief executive, a little more than a week after he resigned amid extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
On Monday, the tech giant’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as president and CEO.
“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said in a statement as the company announced his return.
“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.”
Nvidia said that Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO, will continue as chief financial officer.
United States President Donald Trump welcomed the decision in a post on social media.
“The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. “The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.”
In an interview with CNBC, Trump added that he was “represented in the board meeting” and that his intervention played an important role in the decision. Trump also said he had discussed the shake-up with SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk last week. Trump claimed that Huang “did nothing wrong”.
Democratic and Republican lawmakers have pushed back against the move.
“This reckless decision to bring back Jensen Huang does not change the fact that Huang and NVIDIA still owe Congress answers,” Massachusetts Senator Elizabeth Warren posted on X.
Huang’s resignation on November 12 prompted immediate pushback from Silicon Valley insiders. Within days of his departure, a petition calling for his return had drawn more than 180,000 signatures, including from Musk.
He was reinstated despite multiple investigations under way into the chipmaker, including by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Department of Justice (DOJ).
Nvidia shares jumped by more than 33 percent on the news as US markets opened on Monday.
Analysts also praised the decision. Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager of Founders 100 ETF, told Al Jazeera Huang’s return was a “huge positive”.
“Founders like Jensen are irreplaceable. They bring unparalleled vision, execution and grit. Hard to overstate how important this is for America winning the [super intelligence] race, Nvidia, and innovation in general,” Monaghan said.
“At the end of the day, despite this Jensen saga, the board knew it had no choice but to bring him back, and for the US technology sector, this was the move it had to make,” Dan Ives, senior managing director at Yorkville Ives, said in a note on Monday.
Ives previously said that Nvidia could lose as much as 30 percent of its value without Huang.
The decision coincides with a volatile period for the artificial intelligence (AI) sector following sweeping gains in the recent midterm elections by Democrats, many of whom are more sceptical of AI. The elections also saw voters overwhelmingly reject data centre development in ballot measures held across 10 states.
Last week, Anthropic made its blockbuster Wall Street debut, with shares surging 34 percent from their initial public offering (IPO) price of $83 to $111.50 when trading began. Since then, however, the stock has fallen more than 16 percent.
Nvidia and Anthropic have close financial ties. Nvidia committed $10bn to Anthropic’s IPO, in addition to a separate $10bn investment announced in 2025.
The news has boosted the broader market, which had slumped last week. On Monday, all the major US indices were trending upwards. The tech-heavy Nasdaq was up 6.7 percent, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 2.8 percent and the S&P 500 was up 4.6 percent in early trading.
texts.https://www.wired.com/story/jensen-huang:
Jensen Huang is stepping back into his role as chief executive of Nvidia effective immediately.
The stunning reversal comes 11 days after Huang resigned as CEO from the company he cofounded 33 years ago and after multiple declarations from the board of directors that it had no intention of reinstating him. On Monday, they took a conciliatory tone.
“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers,” said recently appointed board chair Harvey Jones in a press release announcing the decision.
In that announcement the board said it was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia” and that it had “received input from senior levels of the United States government” on the way to its decision. On Monday morning, President Donald Trump posted that the Nvidia board “has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO.”
“I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Huang in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.”
Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on November 12, and longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress was installed as his interim replacement. Five days later, Huang publicly announced that he was open to resuming his role as chief executive, noting the “outpouring of calls” from “employees, investors, business partners, and customers” advocating for his return.
“If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang wrote.
The day Huang resigned, many Nvidia employees spoke up in his support. As reported by WIRED, employees left more than 1,600 comments on an internal “suggestion box” post in which they urged the company’s board to reinstall him as CEO.
In the days following, a public petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement began circulating. At the time of writing, it has amassed more than 200,000 online signatures, the majority of whom self-identified as Nvidia shareholders. Tech elites like Elon Musk and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan have claimed that they were going to sign the petition or had signed it.
Huang’s reinstatement marks a total reversal from the public stance of Nvidia’s board of directors, which said during the company’s November 17 earnings call that it “does not intend” to reinstate him as CEO. WIRED has further reported that the board was alarmed by what one source described as Huang’s “lying” over the last year or so.
President Donald Trump, who developed a close working relationship with Huang during his second administration, had indicated openness to Huang returning as CEO. Trump told reporters on November 16 that he “would not mind” if Huang returned as chief executive, adding that he believed he had “learned a big lesson.”
Huang’s resignation followed days of scrutiny over several extramarital romantic relationships: one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who has no known relation to Jensen, one with an Nvidia employee who directly reported to Huang, and one with a different Nvidia employee.
Huang’s relationship with Alice became the subject of particularly intense focus on November 6, when The New York Times and Financial Times reported that US intelligence officials suspected that Alice may be an asset of the Chinese Ministry of State Security, both citing an intelligence briefing that circulated among top Trump administration officials last year. In the days since, some reports and Trump administration officials have questioned the accuracy of that intelligence. The Chinese government has consistently rejected claims that Alice was one of its spies.
Alice was the chief executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI company that’s been accused of helping Chinese tech companies use Nvidia’s most advanced chips at overseas locations, effectively sidestepping US export restrictions. Alice has also reportedly worked as a television reporter, at HSBC’s Hong Kong-based private banking arm , and at an investment bank backed by the Chinese state.
Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, purportedly with the mission of bringing realistic 3D graphics to personal computers. For many years, the company was primarily known within the gaming community . It didn’t become a household name until the recent AI boom, when its graphics processing units (GPUs) became a crucial piece of infrastructure for powering advanced AI models.
Nvidia controlled about 90 percent of the global GPU market as of September 2026. The year prior, it became the first company to be valued at more than $4 trillion, though its stock price has been in precipitous decline since Huang’s resignation.

The collapse in Turkiye exposes a diplomacy that protects fossil-fuel power while leaving vulnerable countries to pay the price.
Professor of Critical Development Studies at the Faculty of Environmental and Urban Change, York University, Toronto.
COP31 ended without an overarching agreement on Sunday in Antalya, Turkiye, after nearly 200 countries failed to agree on a final climate pact. The proposed text could not even name the principal cause of global warming: fossil fuels. The European Union, several Pacific island states and other governments rejected it, while oil-producing countries resisted stronger language. After three decades of annual summits, this was the first such breakdown since 2009.
It is tempting to call this an extraordinary diplomatic failure. But the collapse reveals something more enduring. Climate negotiations have become remarkably effective at keeping governments at the table while avoiding the economic changes that meaningful climate action requires. The system is not designed literally to produce no agreements; it is designed to accommodate interests powerful enough to prevent decisive ones.
Consider what happened in Antalya. The EU objected that the final draft did not even mention fossil fuels. Yet the omission was not a clerical oversight. Earlier language on moving away from oil, gas and coal had been weakened as negotiations proceeded. The summit could not agree on how to implement the agreement reached at COP28 in Dubai in 2023 to transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems. What should have been the starting point for action became the point at which diplomacy broke down.
The contradiction is built into the negotiating process. Under the Paris Agreement, governments determine their own emissions commitments, with no enforcement mechanism to compel a country to stop expanding fossil-fuel production. COP decisions also depend on consensus, giving determined holdouts considerable leverage. The result is an international forum in which the most reluctant participants can limit what everyone else is allowed to say, let alone do.
That does not mean all countries are equally responsible. Nor does it mean that every COP has achieved nothing. The Paris framework helped establish common goals, and climate summits have encouraged investment and cooperation. Antalya itself adopted limited decisions on other matters, including one on a just transition. But these gains cannot substitute for a credible timetable to wind down fossil-fuel extraction. The distinction matters: diplomatic activity is not the same as structural change.
Indeed, fossil-fuel power operates well beyond the conference hall. Producing states defend revenues and geopolitical influence, while consuming states continue to rely on cheap energy and established infrastructure. Even governments that speak forcefully about climate ambition face incentives to protect their own industries and voters from immediate costs. The global energy transition is therefore not simply a technological problem. It is a struggle over who must relinquish assets, profits and power.
This helps explain the appeal of technological promises. The failed Antalya draft promoted carbon-removal technologies to deal with warming beyond 1.5C, while disagreements also centred on carbon capture and storage. Such approaches may have limited roles in reducing or counterbalancing emissions from difficult-to-abate sectors. But when presented as substitutes for reducing extraction, they allow governments and corporations to promise that future machines will repair the damage of continued emissions. The political benefit is immediate; the promised atmospheric benefit remains uncertain.
The same structural inequality shapes climate finance. Countries that contributed least to historical warming face mounting costs from droughts, floods, displacement and adaptation. Yet the proposed $120bn adaptation target disappeared from the revised text and disputes over financial commitments helped sink the talks. Wealthy governments can celebrate climate ambition while leaving poorer countries to borrow, divert public spending or simply absorb losses.
This is precisely why climate finance cannot be treated as discretionary charity. It concerns responsibility for harms produced through an unequal world economy. Grants, predictable funding and meaningful decision-making power for affected countries are not extras to be negotiated after emissions targets. They are conditions of a transition that poorer countries can undertake without sacrificing education, healthcare and basic development.
There is also a danger in allowing the EU to emerge from Antalya as the uncomplicated defender of climate justice. Its refusal to accept a pact silent on fossil fuels was justified. But wealthy countries cannot demand ambitious language abroad while resisting the financial obligations and domestic changes that would give it substance. Conversely, some developing countries depend on fossil-fuel income or need affordable energy. A just phaseout must distinguish their circumstances from those of rich, historically high-emitting economies.
What would a different climate politics look like? It would begin with enforceable plans for ending new fossil-fuel expansion and phasing down production, with richer countries moving first and fastest. It would fund adaptation and loss and damage through reliable, primarily grant-based transfers rather than debt-creating loans. And it would give countries most vulnerable to climate change greater influence over the decisions that determine their futures.
None of this requires abandoning multilateralism. It requires refusing to confuse its survival with success. When consensus rules repeatedly protect the interests most responsible for the crisis, governments must also pursue complementary agreements, domestic regulation and coalitions willing to move faster. Otherwise, the promise of universal participation becomes a mechanism for universal delay.
The collapse of COP31 is a warning, not because climate diplomacy has suddenly stopped working, but because its limits have become impossible to disguise. The world does not lack knowledge of what causes warming. It lacks a political system willing to confront those who benefit from causing it. Until that changes, each summit will be judged by the agreements it produces, while the atmosphere registers the emissions it fails to prevent.

texts.https://arstechnica.com/science/2026/11/:
COP31 ended without a consensus deal for the first time since 2009.
ANTALYA, Turkey—By the time the United Nations COP31 climate talks ended Sunday afternoon, the conference center resembled a going-out-of-business sale at a pawnshop for broken dreams.
As cleaning crews cleared away the debris left by more than 100,000 participants, Murat Kurum, president of the Conference of the Parties and Turkey’s minister of environment, urbanization, and climate change, tried to tie together disparate parts of a draft climate deal with a shiny ribbon of multilateralism.
For the first time since 2009, the conference ended without consensus on a cover decision, the concluding statement that typically signals global solidarity on how to confront the worsening climate crisis. Countries did adopt several decisions, including a program to help workers and communities transition away from fossil fuels, and a plan to assess progress on climate adaptation.
The failure to agree on an overarching conference statement reflected deep divisions over whether the agreement should mention fossil fuels and carbon capture, as well as how much climate financing developed countries should provide to developing nations hit by costly climate disasters.
The European Union, as well as several Latin American countries and Pacific Island states, said they would not accept the proposed text from the conference leaders.
Cover decisions at the annual conferences usually focus on new steps or language that could reinforce international efforts to slow global warming. A central aim at this meeting was to set quantifiable but voluntary global goals for the widespread electrification of economies, and to increase funding from developed countries to help developing countries adapt to climate impacts.
In 2022, the UN conference in Egypt agreed to establish a loss and damage fund to help vulnerable countries pay for irreversible climate impacts. A year later in Dubai, delegates from more than 190 countries agreed, for the first time, that a “just and orderly” transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems is needed to slow global warming.
Since then, international collaboration on climate issues has declined amid increased conflict, rising oil and gas prices and economic insecurity. The talks in Turkey ran two days beyond the scheduled end without reaching broad agreement on potential next steps, an outcome that won’t kill the global effort but is widely viewed as a serious setback.
But compromise for the sake of consensus is not enough, said Kathy Jetn̄il-Kijiner, a climate envoy for the Marshall Islands Ministry of the Environment.
“We will not be forced to accept false solutions,” she said. “We will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests.” As written, she added, the Antalya Pact undermines her country’s security and threatens its future.
“People are dying, seas are rising, and ecosystems are collapsing,” Jetn̄il-Kijiner said. “Are we so divorced from reality that we take backward steps, even as overshoot threatens to overtake us? To accept this deal would be a betrayal to the Marshallese people.”
It’s not the first time Pacific Island nations threatened by rising seas have objected to the outcome at one of the United Nations’ annual conferences. During the 2023 UN talks in Dubai, a final text was adopted even though a delegation representing 39 small island developing states objected because they were still outside the plenary meeting, trying to coordinate their position.
But in Antalya, the divide ran much deeper. The economically powerful and politically influential European Union, representing 28 member countries, also rejected the proposed agreement.
Ireland’s climate, energy, and environment minister, Darragh O’Brien, said the European countries formally objected to the cover decision because it fell short of what the global climate crisis demands.
“We will not endorse a decision that does not even mention fossil fuels, the key driver of climate change, and not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels,” said O’Brien, speaking on behalf of the EU during Ireland’s rotating presidency.
Egypt and Brazil, hosts of the UN climate talks in 2023 and 2025, also criticized the text proposed by COP31 president Kurum of Turkey and Chris Bowen of Australia, president of the conference negotiations.
Liliam Beatris Chagas de Moura, director for climate at Brazil’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said she was disappointed that this year’s conference did not sustain the momentum from last year’s talks in her country.
Mohammad Ayoub, a climate negotiator with the Saudi Arabian energy ministry, said the 22-member League of Arab States supported the proposed Antalya Pact. He criticized developed countries for using up most of the global carbon budget, the amount of fossil fuels that can be burned without overheating the planet, and then asking developing countries to give up the very energy sources that fueled their own growth.
Ayoub condemned some countries’ opposition to including references to carbon dioxide removal and carbon capture and storage in the pact, calling their resistance to those technologies unscientific.
Carbon capture and storage are not close to being deployed fast enough “to keep 1.5 degrees within reach,” he said, referring to the long-term goal of limiting the average global temperature increase established by the 2015 Paris climate agreement.
“We believe that climate change requires all solutions on the table, and that countries select from these solutions depending on their national circumstances.”
UN Secretary-General António Guterres said he was “deeply disappointed” that the talks ended without consensus on an overarching agreement.
“But this setback does not change the facts,” he said. “Fossil fuels are driving the climate crisis. We can’t put out the fire while pouring fuel on it.”
Bob Berwyn is an Austria-based reporter who has covered climate science and international climate policy for more than a decade. Previously, he reported on the environment, endangered species, and public lands for several Colorado newspapers, and also worked as editor and assistant editor at community newspapers in the Colorado Rockies.

Best Traditional Espresso Machine in our guide to the best , the Mio is stylish and built to last, with an analog design and a two-year warranty. It also makes for a solid first “real” espresso machine with its built-in shot timer and pressure gauge.
Fellow set some pretty lofty expectations with the release of its sleek Aiden coffee maker in 2024 , and according to former WIRED reviewer Matthew Korfhage , the brand didn't disappoint on its first attempt at an espresso machine. The ability to adjust flow rates and pressure curves was once the province of, as Korfhage put it, only the “richest and nerdiest of nerds.” But Fellow now allows you—yes, you, at home in your kitchen—to fine-tune how water moves through the grounds, unlocking previously unforeseen dimensions of flavor.
When we tested this machine , we liked it for a variety of reasons, including an easy-to-use milk frother and two swappable bean hoppers, which are especially helpful if you like to switch to decaf in the afternoons. It comes in a variety of finishes, but note that Beige is the cheapest of all right now, at only $915 .
This flashy, design-oriented semiautomatic (“a steampunk gasworks of a thing ,” according to Korfhage) is quite dramatic in person. It has a dual boiler—meaning you can froth milk at the same time you’re pulling a shot—and it comes with a nice set of accessories, including a tamper and milk pitcher. Note that this sale is on the 2nd Gen machine, which features expanded grinder settings and a new portafilter.
Formerly the Linea Classic, De’Longhi’s Classic is the best bare-bones espresso machine we’ve tried , with a pressure gauge, 15-bar pump, and updated thermoblock system. I used one for a full year and, while it’s not as foolproof as a semiautomatic, it was easy enough for morning espresso shots and cappuccinos; I even pulled off some rudimentary latte art with its steam wand.
The Vertuo Pop+ is our favorite pod maker for espresso . The Deluxe model adds a larger, side-mount water tank (37 ounces to the original’s 25 ounces) and new finishes, including this white one, a matte black-and-gold, and a sort of gunmetal gray.
We appreciated this semiautomatic’s slim profile, consistent shots, and built-in burr grinder. The cold-brew setting is more of a gimmick than a way to make actual cold brew, and some design choices are a bit quirky. Even so, it’s a beautiful, industrial-looking machine that takes up only 12 inches of counter space.
Ninja sometimes has a reputation for doing too much, but we liked this semiautomatic as a beginner-friendly option that pulls some solid shots. It’s got a built-in grinder and milk frother, the latter of which can make cold foam and even has a setting for plant-based milk. In true Ninja fashion, it also has settings for drip coffee and cold brew, but neither impressed our tester, so I wouldn’t buy it for those features alone.
Former WIRED reviewer Matthew Korfhage tested Terra Kaffe's newer Demi and said it was perhaps the “dead-simplest fully automatic espresso machine I've yet encountered that still makes good coffee,” with just a dial and a button. Right now it's $200 off, or $300 off with a coffee subscription (Terra-Kaffe offers a house blend specifically made for use on its machines). Its bigger sibling, the TK-02, impressed our tester with its convenience, ease of use, front-facing water filter, and milk carafe. Though it didn't come out on top during a blind espresso taste test we did earlier this year , it's still a great-looking machine that's easy to use and is a whopping $400 off (or $500 with a coffee subscription) for Black Friday.
Maybe you or your recipient already has an espresso machine; in that case, they’ll need some quality beans. Our favorite coffee subscription , Atlas Coffee Club, has a new gift option on offer for Black Friday : a quarterly subscription of three bags of unique, globally sourced coffee every three months for $59 . You can choose any roast you want, including espresso roast and even Nespresso pods. If you’d rather buy an ongoing subscription for yourself, your first bag is free with Atlas’ Black Friday sale.
Former barista and WIRED contributing reviewer Pete Cottell likes this little scale that includes three magnetic add-ons: a platform, a metal dosing cup, and a catch cup that fits directly onto almost any portafilter.
If grounds are sticking to the plastic components of your coffee grinder, Cottell recommends adding this durable, stylish spray bottle to your espresso setup.
Cottell likes situating this mat underneath your espresso setup, as the lip contains spills and the textured portion is great for drying tools post-washing.
Some machines come with a tamper; others don't. If yours doesn’t, Cottell recommends you get this one . The spring-loaded base unloads 15 pounds of force to create a perfectly flat puck inside your portafilter. (A click lets you know when to stop pushing, so it’s great for beginners, too.)

Black Friday is in less than a week away, and deals on Apple devices, games, robovacs, and more are already here.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
The countdown to Black Friday is on, and many discounts have already arrived. Although the shopping holiday isn’t officially until Friday, November 27th, retailers are already dropping early deals on some of our favorite tech. Of course, with prices rising across the board, a good discount doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting a historically low price. But we’re still seeing worthwhile discounts on a wide variety of tried-and-tested gear, with more expected later this week.
Below, we’ve rounded up the best early Black Friday deals we’ve found so far. Prices could drop further as Black Friday approaches, as is always the case, but these deals are worth considering if you’d rather shop early and beat the holiday rush. We’ll continue to update this guide as more retailers launch their holiday sales, too, so be sure to check back regularly as we get closer to the main event.
Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review .
An HBO Max Basic subscription provides access to shows like House of the Dragon, The Last of Us, and The Pitt , as well as films like Superman and Weapons. You can get a year of the monthly, ad-supported subscription for $2.99 ($8 off) a month until December 1st.
The Nintendo Switch 2 features a 7.9-inch LCD display, magnetically attached Joy-Con 2 controllers, backward compatibility with most original Switch games, and exclusive titles like Donkey Kong Bananza and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Read our review .
Do you ever wish you could turn on your coffee maker or hit the light switch without getting up? The SwitchBot Bot lets you do that. All you need to do is stick the inexpensive contraption on a standard button or rocker switch, which will allow you to control or schedule your pet feeder, garage door, and a wide range of other devices from your smartphone.
Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.
Amazon’s last-gen Fire TV Stick 4K Plus streams in 4K and supports Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision, and Alexa Plus. It also ships with the redesigned Fire OS and, unlike more recent models, still lets you sideload Android TV apps.
Sony’s last-last-gen noise-canceling headphones were so good, the company brought them back with a few minor improvements. They still offer great ANC, a timeless foldable design, and a 10-band EQ, delivering performance nearly on par with Sony’s newer flagships at a fraction of the cost.
Lego’s miniature bonsai trees can bring a sense of calm to even the most cluttered home. Building each tree — whether it be the black pine, the ginkgo, or the lilac-adorned wisteria — is designed to be a mindfulness practice in itself, centering your giftee as they go. They also make for a great piece of decor once finished, adding a touch of zen to any desk or shelf.
Rechargeable AA batteries are handy, until it’s time to charge them. Most wall chargers let you refill four, maybe six, at once. Zepath’s clever solution is to ship them in a easy-to-use USB-C charging case that charges eight simultaneously. The batteries themselves are long-lasting, too.
Sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.
The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review .

It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.
Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.

JBL’s Tour One M3 noise-canceling headphones come with a touchscreen-equipped wireless transmitter that lets you wirelessly listen to audio from in-flight entertainment systems and other devices without Bluetooth. They also offer solid active noise cancellation and last up to 70 hours on a charge.
Hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.
The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is a beginner-friendly 3D printer that supports four filament spools. It features an enclosed build chamber, automatic bed leveling, and a large touchscreen, making it easy to produce reliable prints.

There's no denying that 2026 has been a slower year for the iPad lineup . Only the iPad Air and iPad Mini received updates (with nothing new for the iPad or iPad Pro since 2025), and in June, the entire lineup was subject to a painful price hike of either $100 or $200, depending on the model. But that's not to say you need to abandon your dreams of getting a good deal on a great iPad this year.
In the lead-up to Black Friday, there are already some solid sales that make now a smart time to shop for an iPad. For more shopping advice from our team of product testers and deal hunters, check out our Best Early Black Friday Deals , Best Amazon Early Black Friday Deals , and Best Early Black Friday Laptop Deals .
Even though it's more than two years old at this point, the 2024 iPad Mini is the best iPad deal ahead of Black Friday. It's $100 off, bringing the price down to $499. That's just $50 more than the base iPad (the most affordable in the lineup), below. With its tiny size and weight, the iPad Mini is the perfect device to take on the go with you. You can also conveniently use it one-handed, which is especially helpful if you're using an Apple Pencil Pro in your other hand. Don't get me wrong: The improvements to the newer iPad Mini are substantial and worthwhile to the right person. The updated OLED screen is gorgeous; the chassis is even thinner; and the front-facing camera is better for video calls, having been moved to the side bezel. But because it's $300 more expensive, most people should stick with the older model—especially since the iPad Mini is better-suited for more casual tasks, like reading and note-taking.
If you're trying to save the most cash, the base iPad is the absolute cheapest. You might appreciate the larger screen over the iPad Mini, too. While $50 isn't a huge discount—and it's also a fairly common price—hopefully we'll see deeper cuts in the future. Even so, this is a good buy right now, particularly if you're looking for a tablet to use immediately, whether for an upcoming flight or to keep kids busy on a long car trip.
The iPad Air is the in-between iPad. It's not as cheap as the base iPad, nor does it have the Tandem OLED screen and high-end features of the iPad Pro. And yet, I find that it's the iPad people should buy if they intend to use it for work. That's primarily because it has both a powerful M4 chip and can be connected to a Magic Keyboard with full trackpad support. The most recent versions of iPadOS make windowing much easier, and Apple even made the cursor work more like macOS. After all, most people don't need an OLED screen to do some word processing, answer emails, and take the occasional Zoom call.
When you're ready to use it more like a traditional tablet, just pull it off its magnetic cover, and it's ready for your fingers or an Apple Pencil. The 11-inch model is still small enough to not feel overwhelming in your hands. And while the $649 sale isn't particularly rare, it's not a bad price for a tablet that functions pretty well as a laptop replacement.
iPad Mini (2026) for $599 ($100 off) : The latest iPad Mini came out just last month, and this is the first time it's gone on sale. It's a significant upgrade from the 2024 iPad Mini, with its OLED display and improved performance. But as a small, one-handed tablet, the previous-gen iPad Mini (A17 Pro) for $499 is the better deal right now—and the smart buy for most.
iPad Pro 11-inch for $1,099 : It's a little surprising that the iPad Pro hasn't been discounted at all for Black Friday. At $1,099, it's cheaper than the 13-inch MacBook Air, which uses the same M5 chip. The difference? You still have to buy the Magic Keyboard separately to pair with the iPad Pro. All in all, the iPad ends up being a much more expensive device.

AMD , yapay zeka modellerinin çalıştırılmasına yönelik özel çipler geliştiren Taalas 'ı yaklaşık 2,9 milyar dolar değerindeki bir anlaşmayla satın aldı . AMD'nin söz konusu teknolojiyi Instinct hızlandırıcı ürün ailesine dahil etmeyi planladığı belirtiliyor.
2023 yılında Toronto'da kurulan Taalas, yapay zeka modellerine özel çipler geliştiriyor. Ljubiša Bajić , Lejla Bajić ve Drago Ignjatović tarafından kurulan şirket, genel amaçlı GPU'lar yerine belirli yapay zeka modellerini temel alan bir donanım yaklaşımı benimsiyor. Bu yaklaşımda yapay zeka modelleri doğrudan silikon üzerine entegre ediliyor. Böylece modellerin çıkarım (inference) süreçlerinin daha hızlı ve verimli hale getirilmesi hedefleniyor.
Taalas'ın ilk demonstrasyon çipi, Meta'nın Llama 3.1 8B modeli için geliştirildi. Şirketin açıklamalarına göre çip, kullanıcı başına saniyede yaklaşık 17 bin token işleyebiliyor. AMD'nin satın alma sonrasında bu teknolojiyi Instinct hızlandırıcı yol haritasına dahil etmesi bekleniyor.
Şirket bugüne kadar Quiet Capital, Lamond Ventures, Fidelity ve Belgrad merkezli Fifth Quarter Ventures (5QV) gibi yatırımcılardan yaklaşık 220 milyon dolar yatırım aldı. Taalas, Fifth Quarter Ventures'ın ilk fonu kapsamında yatırım yaptığı erken aşama şirketler arasında yer alıyor.

State AGs called the weak safeguards built into Elon Musk’s AI image generator ‘not a failure but a feature.’
In separate but similar lawsuits filed on Monday, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones accused SpaceX of violating state consumer protection laws by ignoring industry-standard safeguards and falsely promoting the safety of its X social media platform and Grok AI features. The complaint filed in Virginia accuses Musk of willfully ignoring growing concerns around AI-generated sexualized deepfakes, and “instead saw a market opportunity for more profits,” describing the weak safeguards around Grok as “not a failure but a feature.”
“Time and again, xAI and X told consumers they were being protected from abuses. That was false. Instead, the tool permitted users to routinely create and circulate non-consensual intimate imagery and sexualized images, and child sexual abuse material (CSAM), causing harm to individuals and children,” Jones said in a press statement . “Companies that deploy powerful tools don’t get to ignore consumer safety and call it innovation.”
The complaints largely center around Grok Imagine, a tool that allows Grok and X users to generate images and videos. In August 2025, Grok maker xAI (which Musk has since merged with SpaceX ) launched a “spicy” mode for Grok Imagine that spat out sexualized content including nude deepfakes of celebrities like Taylor Swift. In January 2026, Grok gained a feature that allowed X users to instantly edit any image without requiring consent from the original poster — resulting in X becoming flooded with nonconsensual, sexualized deepfakes of adults and minors .
xAI made several changes to restrict access to Grok image editing, moving some capabilities behind a paywall and blocking certain requests for sexual poses, swimwear, or explicit scenarios. Our testing at the Verge following these restriction updates found they did little to prevent the bot from creating sexualized deepfakes, however.
Both of the Oregon and Virginia lawsuits are seeking financial damages.
The X Safety team said in a statement released after the lawsuits were announced that it takes appropriate measures to address users who generate sexual content involving minors:
“The people who tried to use Grok Imagine to generate this material did so by deliberately violating our Terms of Service and working aggressively to circumvent our safeguards. When some of these bad actors found ways to misuse Grok Imagine earlier this year, we acted promptly to tighten its protections, which are designed to refuse any request to generate explicit images of minors or real people. To stay ahead of this disgusting and indefensible conduct, we keep testing and adjusting those protections as these abusers change tactics. We also implement sophisticated classifiers that screen every prompt before an image is generated and check every output after.”
